newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to sell off stakes in two wine firms.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to sell off stakes in two wine firms.

text.p: Morocco plans to sell off up to 80 percent of state stakes in Sincomar and Serecaf companies, the country's main wine production, distribution and storing firms, Attijari Finances stockbroker said on Friday.

"The Privatisation Ministry plans to put its 80 percent in Sincomar and 74 percent in Serecaf firms for sale in the second half of 1997," Youssef Rouissi, an analyst at Ittijari Finances told Reuters.
Local and foreign investors interested in the offer "should get in touch with us before June 20, 1997," he added.
Attijari Finance, chosen by the ministry as adviser for the privatisation operation, is known as the brokerage house of Morocco's leading Banque Commerciale du Maroc.
Established in 1946 in Casablanca, Sincomar controls nearly 50 percent of Morocco's wine total production estimated at 300,000 hectolitres per year.
Morocco has an estimated 6,500 hectares of wine-growing areas.
According to official statistics, Sincomar exports some of its wine products to North America, Africa and Europe, mainly France.
Privatisation of wine units, is a part of the undergoing government plan to sell 113 state-owned firms to privates by end of 1998.
